programme.desc: Henry MooreHuw Wheldon visits Henry Moore at his home in the run-up to a major exhibition of his work at the Whitechapel Gallery in London. Wheldon tries to uncover meanings and motivations in the artist's work, but Moore freely admits that he doesn't want to examine himself too thoroughly in case it inhibits his ability to create. "I hate talking about my work", said Moore. "You can't explain a year's work in five minutes; and in any case all you do is to release your tensions and talk them away.".

programme.title: Eternals
programme.desc: When monstrous entities called Deviants infest the Earth in 5000 BC Mesopotamia, an ancient race of beings known as Celestials, led by the mighty Arishem, fashion humanity's superpowered protectors, the Eternals. For more than 7,000 years, this band of near-immortal saviours live among us, in plain sight but unseen. They are instructed not to interfere in human conflicts unless Deviants are involved, and watch with dismay as humans resolve differences with bloodshed. Sci-fi adventure from Marvel Studios, starring Gemma Chan, Richard Madden, Angelina Jolie and Salma Hayek.

programme.title: Mary Poppins Returns
programme.desc: In 1930s London, Michael Banks lives in his family home with his children, Annabel, John, and Georgie. Still grieving the death of his wife, and behind on loan payments, his house is due to be repossessed unless he comes up with the money soon. Thankfully, help comes in the form of the practically perfect nanny who returns 25 years after her previous visit. Musical fantasy, starring Emily Blunt, Dick Van Dyke and Meryl Streep.

programme.title: Ralph Breaks the Internet
programme.desc: Six years after the events of Wreck-It Ralph, the destructive video game character and his hyperactive friend Vanellope discover a wi-fi router in Litwak's Family Fun Centre and Arcade. Before long, they embark on a new quest involving Disney princesses, and a few familar faces. Animated adventure, with the voices of John C Reilly, Sarah Silverman and Gal Gadot.

programme.title: Lilo & Stitch
programme.desc: A lonely little girl befriends a runaway alien that helps mend her fractured family. Live action fantasy adventure, starring Maia Kealoha and Sydney Agudong.

programme.title: Cars 2
programme.desc: Racing car Lightning McQueen heads overseas to compete in an international grand prix, with events in Britain, Japan and Italy. He gets mixed up in international espionage when a case of mistaken identity leads to an encounter with two English spy cars searching for a powerful gadget. Pixar animated adventure sequel, with the voices of Owen Wilson and Michael Caine.

programme.title: Beauty and the Beast
programme.desc: A prince is transformed into a hideous monster as punishment for his selfishness, and can only regain his human form by finding true love. Salvation comes in the form of a spirited village girl, who offers to take her father's place when he is imprisoned in the monster's castle. But as romance blossoms between the unlikely pair, a jealous rival suitor only sees a beast to be slain. Live-action remake of the Disney animated fairy tale, starring Emma Watson, Dan Stevens and Luke Evans, with Ewan McGregor, Emma Thompson and Ian McKellen playing the Beast's entourage of living ornaments.

programme.title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua
programme.desc: A pampered pet dog gets separated from her owner, and is left stranded in Mexico struggling to avoid a dognapper and a ferocious Doberman, who are after her diamond collar. Luckily, a courageous German shepherd is on hand to help her get back home. Comedy, starring Piper Perabo and Jamie Lee Curtis, with the voices of Drew Barrymore and Andy Garcia.

programme.title: The Lion King
programme.desc: After the murder of his father Mufasa, young lion prince Simba flees his African kingdom, only to learn the true meaning of responsibility and bravery as he clashes with his wicked uncle Scar. Director Jon Favreau's animated remake of Disney's 1994 blockbuster, featuring the voices of Donald Glover, Beyonce Knowles and Seth Rogen.

programme.title: Raya and the Last Dragon
programme.desc: Chief Benja and his 'dragon nerd' daughter Raya proudly protect a luminescent stone that protects humanity from a plague borne of discord called the Druun. One poor judgement allows the darkness to return, and Raya embarks on a perilous quest to restore peace by completing a series of Indiana-Jones-style obstacles. Animated fantasy, with the voices of Kelly Marie Tran, Awkwafina, Izaac Wang and Gemma Chan.

He intercedes in this struggle after rescuing a princess from captivity, and must win the trust of a fierce primitive tribe to save the world. Fantasy adventure based on Edgar Rice Burroughs' series of novels, starring Taylor Kitsch and Lynn Collins.

programme.desc: A deskbound CIA agent provides valuable background support for a dashing secret agent, but has never gone into action herself. Everything changes, when the spy mysteriously vanishes, and she leaps into action to take his place, infiltrating the inner circle of a ruthless arms dealer and trying to avert a global catastrophe. Comedy adventure, starring Melissa McCarthy, Jason Statham and Rose Byrne.

programme.desc: Courageous military recruits hurl themselves into a desperate war against alien insects set on destroying mankind. They blast off for the creatures' home planet in a last-ditch attempt to save the human race from annihilation - little realising the carnage that awaits them. Sci-fi adventure from director Paul Verhoeven, starring Casper Van Dien, Denise Richards and Dina Meyer.

Fantasy adventure sequel, starring Ben Barnes, William Moseley, Georgie Henley, Skandar Keynes, Anna Popplewell and Peter Dinklage.

Disney animated musical fantasy, with the voices of Anika Noni Rose and Bruno Campos.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: S2 E5 — DerryDermot O'Leary visits Londonderry, where he heads to the Walled City brewery to find out about the local ingredient behind their standout brews. He then gets in a kayak to take in the skyline from a whole new angle, before getting hands-on with chef Kevin Pyke at Pyke 'N' Pommes, preparing calamari and building tacos.

programme.title: Gary Barlow's Food and Wine Tour: New Zealand
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Marlborough SoundsGary and Jason Manford head to Havelock, gateway to the Marlborough Sounds, where local seafood entrepreneur Maegan Blom takes them through a spectacular maze of sheltered waterways, forested hills and peaceful bays. They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. Then they drive their camper van to Picton to board a ferry for the scenic Cook Strait crossing from the South Island to the North Island, heading up to the bridge to meet the captain, before enjoying a sunny beer-tasting out on deck.

programme.title: The Joy of Pets
programme.desc: S1 E4Gaby Roslin and vet Bolu Eso are in Birmingham celebrating the extraordinary bond between people and animals. At a specialist veterinary hospital, Bolu follows Labrador Bobbie as he undergoes pioneering laser surgery, while another dog presents the team with a neurological mystery. Gaby learns about StreetVet, the charity providing free veterinary care to the pets of people experiencing homelessness.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E12 — Plantation CountryThe chef visits Louisiana, cooks in the historic Houmas House, and samples local speciality gumbo, courtesy of the resident cook. He is also taken on a ghost tour to find out about people who once worked on the property.

programme.title: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
programme.desc: Sci-fi adventure starring Jeff Goldblum and Julianne Moore. Past experience tells Dr Ian Malcolm not to get involved with businessman John Hammond's new scheme to build a dinosaur park. However, he reluctantly agrees when he realises that his girlfriend is already on site. On his arrival on the secluded island he soon finds that his fears were well founded.

programme.title: 7 Up: The Story
programme.desc: In 1964, ITV broadcast a film about 14 seven-year-olds, which became the longest-running documentary series ever. It set out to prove that Britain was divided by the class system and that these children's futures had been decided by the street they were born on. This programme looks at the year 7 Up was made, the idea behind it, and what the subjects hoped for in a Britain about to change around them.

They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. programme.desc: S1 E4Gaby Roslin and vet Bolu Eso are in Birmingham celebrating the extraordinary bond between people and animals. Gaby learns about StreetVet, the charity providing free veterinary care to the pets of people experiencing homelessness.

programme.desc: S2 E5 — DerryDermot O'Leary visits Londonderry, where he heads to the Walled City brewery to find out about the local ingredient behind their standout brews. He then gets in a kayak to take in the skyline from a whole new angle, before getting hands-on with chef Kevin Pyke at Pyke 'N' Pommes, preparing calamari and building tacos.

programme.title: Gary Barlow's Food and Wine Tour: New Zealand
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Marlborough SoundsGary and Jason Manford head to Havelock, gateway to the Marlborough Sounds, where local seafood entrepreneur Maegan Blom takes them through a spectacular maze of sheltered waterways, forested hills and peaceful bays. They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. Then they drive their camper van to Picton to board a ferry for the scenic Cook Strait crossing from the South Island to the North Island, heading up to the bridge to meet the captain, before enjoying a sunny beer-tasting out on deck.

programme.title: The Joy of Pets
programme.desc: S1 E4Gaby Roslin and vet Bolu Eso are in Birmingham celebrating the extraordinary bond between people and animals. At a specialist veterinary hospital, Bolu follows Labrador Bobbie as he undergoes pioneering laser surgery, while another dog presents the team with a neurological mystery. Gaby learns about StreetVet, the charity providing free veterinary care to the pets of people experiencing homelessness.

programme.title: Gary Barlow's Food and Wine Tour: New Zealand
programme.desc: S1 E5 — Marlborough SoundsGary and Jason Manford head to Havelock, gateway to the Marlborough Sounds, where local seafood entrepreneur Maegan Blom takes them through a spectacular maze of sheltered waterways, forested hills and peaceful bays. They drop anchor at her working mussel farm to see how greenshell mussels are grown, before heading back to shore for meal. Then they drive their camper van to Picton to board a ferry for the scenic Cook Strait crossing from the South Island to the North Island, heading up to the bridge to meet the captain, before enjoying a sunny beer-tasting out on deck.

programme.title: The Joy of Pets
programme.desc: S1 E4Gaby Roslin and vet Bolu Eso are in Birmingham celebrating the extraordinary bond between people and animals. At a specialist veterinary hospital, Bolu follows Labrador Bobbie as he undergoes pioneering laser surgery, while another dog presents the team with a neurological mystery. Gaby learns about StreetVet, the charity providing free veterinary care to the pets of people experiencing homelessness.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E12 — Plantation CountryThe chef visits Louisiana, cooks in the historic Houmas House, and samples local speciality gumbo, courtesy of the resident cook. He is also taken on a ghost tour to find out about people who once worked on the property.

programme.title: The Lost World: Jurassic Park
programme.desc: Sci-fi adventure starring Jeff Goldblum and Julianne Moore. Past experience tells Dr Ian Malcolm not to get involved with businessman John Hammond's new scheme to build a dinosaur park. However, he reluctantly agrees when he realises that his girlfriend is already on site. On his arrival on the secluded island he soon finds that his fears were well founded.

programme.title: U-Boat Wargamers
programme.desc: E3When Gilbert Roberts arrives to set up a tactical school for the U-boats, he receives a frosty reception from Admiral Noble. Enlisting the help of Jean Laidlaw and a small team of Wrens, Roberts begins unpicking the flaws in Walker’s ‘Buttercup’.

programme.title: U-Boat Wargamers
programme.desc: E4Roberts and Laidlaw have uncovered a flaw in the Royal Navy’s anti-U-boat tactic ‘Buttercup’. By wargaming through different scenarios, they develop a counter-tactic of their own, Codenamed operation ‘Raspberry’.

programme.title: U-Boat Wargamers
programme.desc: E5Karl Dönitz fills the ocean with wolfpacks. It's 1943, and with supplies spread thin, pressure mounts on Roberts and the Wrens as they fight to prove the their tactics. Convoy ONS. 5 catches Dönitz’s attention, setting the stage for a pivotal battle.

programme.title: U-Boat Wargamers
programme.desc: E6WATU faces a crucial encounter for ONS.5 in the Battle of the Atlantic. Dönitz unleashes the new torpedo that targets the escort ships. Roberts and Laidlaw must counteract the new weapon and recapture the waves.

programme.title: History Of Weapons

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E2Examining how warfare entered a new dimension as attacks from the skies became possible with weapons from incendiary arrows to drones.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E3Weapons experts test the physical and psychological impact of close combat weapons - the Roman short sword, the medieval war hammer and the bayonet.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E4From the crossbow to the Kalashnikov to 3D-printed firearms, weaponry designed for everyone can offer a decisive advantage in warfare.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E5In spectacular experiments, a team of international experts presents the most significant cases in the history of weapons where speed has made a decisive difference.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E6New weapons with devastating force shape the wars of the 20th century. International experts test the catastrophic effects of the three most destructive weapons of our time: the machine gun, hand grenade and tank.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E7A look at key maritime weapons such as the secret super-weapon that kept Constantinople safe for centuries, the thunderous force of a ship's cannon, and the deadly torpedo.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E8Examining how the techniques of ambush, along with weapons that remained undetected until the very moment they were used, would revolutionise warfare.

programme.title: History Of Weapons
programme.desc: E9Wars become even bloodier as new technologies continue to evolve. An international team of experts tests the deadliest weapons upgrades in the history of warfare.

programme.desc: E10Experts look at three types of weapon employed to attack civilian populations, from the medieval trebuchet to modern bio-weapons and nuclear bombs.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4Destroyers and Cruisers showcases ships that with their speed and firepower became the backbones of 20th century navies. We tell the incredible story of USS Laffey, the WW2 destroyer that would come to be known as ‘the ship that would not die’.

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered
programme.desc: E1In 1944, 28 Greek socialists were shot in Syntagma Square and 100,000 had perished by the end of the Civil War. Was this the old order Winston Churchill had longed for?

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered
programme.desc: E2Since the Syrian civil war broke out in 2011, 400,000 have been killed in the conflict. Who is to blame for this and the terrible conditions in which its people live?

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The F15 Eagle immediately turned the tide of the first Gulf War to prove its greatness. Our immaculately restored MiG Killer was involved in one of the most bizarre combat incidents during that conflict, and has survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2The mighty Flying Fortress takes to the air as we examine the background and development of one of WWIIs most iconic bombers. Serving with both the USAAF and the RAF, we see it in action and fly a surfing example.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E2Veterans and historians of the Thai-Burma railway tell the story of its construction. Built to supply Japan’s invasion of India, it cost thousands of lives – both POWs and Asian slave labourers.

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E6Two of the fastest combat aircraft of World War 2, their origins couldn't differ more. The Messerschmitt 262 was the brainchild of genius designer Willy Messerschmitt and it became the first combat jet in history.

programme.title: Iconic Combat Machines
programme.desc: E5The Soviet Union produced a large variety of tanks and airplanes during World War II. What made the T34 and the Chaika stand out and become icons?

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The Hawker Hurricane was the first RAF aircraft to fly over 300mph. Over half of every enemy aeroplane destroyed in the Battle of Britain was by a Hurricane, not a Spitfire.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II. Regarded as one of the most important aircraft of the Cold War. It was a major part of the United States Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps, and was also used by many other countries.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E4In the 19th century, weapons became more sophisticated and more deadly, and the results were higher casualties with devastating wounds.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E11By early 1945, the end was in sight. After months of hard fighting the Allies were advancing towards the Rhine and to the east the Russians were closing in on Berlin as part of Operation Bagration.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E12The conflict in the Pacific provided history with some of the worst reminders of the true meaning of war. Even today the images captured on islands such as Iwo Jima and Okinawa have the power to shock a world by the horrors of more recent events.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E9The decision by Hitler to send his armies east in to Russia was probably the most significant of the war. Now against military convention, he was fighting on two fronts and almost as bad made a bitter enemy of an erstwhile ally.

programme.title: Wwii: Witness To War
programme.desc: E10And so it finally arrived: 6th June 1944, the day that British, US and Canadian troops were sent across the English Channel to begin the job of reclaiming continental Europe and freeing it from German occupation.

programme.title: The Last Burma Star
programme.desc: E1To mark the 80th anniversary of VJ Day, explorer Levison Wood and historian Alex Bescoby set out on an urgent mission to honour the last surviving veterans of the Burma Campaign – the brutal, often forgotten chapter of the Second World War.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The aircraft capable of delivering the payload of a B17, in a single post war air frame. The many variants of this single piston engined fighter bomber helped dominate the air to ground attack role in Vietnam, earning quite a reputation.

programme.desc: E5This episode tells stories about the secret world of naval deception and cloak and dagger missions. 1914, the yacht Asgard, manned by Erskine Childers, smuggled rifles into a fishing village to arm an Irish militia in their struggle for Home Rule.
